title: Maxwell sells Promis software to Sandia

tellings.quote: So, he sold that to Sandia Labs.

plain: The story goes that in the 1980s the British media owner Robert Maxwell sold a computer program called Promis, a piece of data-tracking software, to Sandia Labs, a US government weapons laboratory in New Mexico. A researcher named Jason Simosa, who also counts himself a witness, tells it without naming a source: "So, he sold that to Sandia Labs." He tells it because it would put a foreign businessman's software inside one of America's most secret labs.
